main_text.p: 12 Hujus artis imago ab homine recepta duas alias artes secundarias & sibi ancillantes parit, quibus ab homine ad hominem deferri possit, Grammaticam & Rhetoricam.
13 Istæ tres artes sunt generales, quia in omnibus rebus & artibus usum habent
14 In ipso Ente reali est, limitatio per quantitatem, actus per naturam, & finis quæ bonitas appellatur.

15 Quantitatis artes sunt Mathemati- ce, Naturæ Physica, Bonitatis Theologia: sed Theologiæ non nisi tenuia principia in rebus creatis insunt, aut ex ipsis colligi possunt: quoniam irrationales creaturæ, quamvis Deum versus tendunt, qui est primum & summum bonum, ad ipsum tamen non attingunt. Homini igitur doctrina seu revelatione divina opus est, ultra vestigia illa bonitatis quæ in creaturis adumbrantur, ut bene vivendo ad Deum ascendat.
16 Harum omnium artium comprehensio, qua res emanant ab ente primo, & ad ipsum denuo redeunt, Encyclopædia nominatur: cujus catenæ circularis primus annulus est Dialectica, & ultimus Theologia.

page.notes: The leading mark before "cepta" in the second paragraph line is probably a printed or dirt mark; it is not transcribed. The page is cut off at the bottom and the right side; the continuation is in part 2. The numbers 11 to 15 are printed in small roman numerals and are copied as the Arabic equivalents. The upper part of the page and the left portion of the lines are cut off in this part; the signature A 3 and the catchword DE- are printed at the foot. The gutter strip at left shows partial lines of the facing page, not transcribed.
